requirements.quote: Padding octets MUST be set to zero when sending.  A receiver is
requirements.condition: When sending padding octets
requirements.required_behavior: Set every padding octet to zero.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded padding octets can be inspected for a zero value.

requirements.quote:
not obligated to verify padding but MAY treat non-zero padding as
      a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a receiver detects non-zero padding
requirements.error_behavior: The receiver is permitted to treat the condition as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime test can send non-zero padding and accept either tolerance or the explicitly permitted connection error.

requirements.quote:
PADDED (0x08):  When set, the PADDED flag indicates that the Pad
      Length field and any padding that it describes are present.
requirements.condition: When the PUSH_PROMISE PADDED flag (0x08) is set
requirements.required_behavior: The Pad Length field and the padding it describes are present.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Omit the Pad Length field or its described padding.
requirements.why_checkable: A frame parser or serializer can verify the conditional presence of the Pad Length field and padding.

requirements.quote:
END_HEADERS (0x04):  When set, the END_HEADERS flag indicates that
      this frame contains an entire field block (Section 4.3) and is not
      followed by any CONTINUATION frames.
requirements.condition: When the PUSH_PROMISE END_HEADERS flag (0x04) is set
requirements.required_behavior: The frame contains the entire field block.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Follow the frame with a CONTINUATION frame for that field block.
requirements.why_checkable: The field-block completeness and absence of subsequent CONTINUATION frames can be checked from the frame sequence.

requirements.quote:
A PUSH_PROMISE frame without the END_HEADERS flag set MUST be
      followed by a CONTINUATION frame for the same stream.  A receiver
requirements.condition: When a PUSH_PROMISE frame does not have END_HEADERS set
requirements.required_behavior: Immediately follow it with a CONTINUATION frame on the same stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Terminate or continue the field block with a frame other than CONTINUATION or on another stream.
requirements.why_checkable: The next frame's type and stream identifier can be compared with the PUSH_PROMISE frame.

requirements.quote:
MUST treat the receipt of any other type of frame or a frame on a
      different stream as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
      PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: After a PUSH_PROMISE without END_HEADERS, when the next frame is not CONTINUATION or is on a different stream
requirements.error_behavior: Treat receipt as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime test can inject an invalid intervening frame type or stream identifier and observe the connection error.

requirements.quote:
PUSH_PROMISE frames MUST only be sent on a peer-initiated stream that
   is in either the "open" or "half-closed (remote)" state.  The stream
requirements.condition: When sending a PUSH_PROMISE frame
requirements.required_behavior: Send it only on a peer-initiated stream in the open or half-closed (remote) state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send it on a locally initiated stream or a stream in any other state.
requirements.why_checkable: The associated stream's initiator and state can be inspected when the frame is emitted.

requirements.quote:
identifier of a PUSH_PROMISE frame indicates the stream it is
   associated with.  If the Stream Identifier field specifies the value
   0x00, a recipient MUST respond with a connection error
   (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a PUSH_PROMISE frame has Stream Identifier 0x00
requirements.error_behavior: Respond with a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A malformed PUSH_PROMISE with stream identifier zero can be injected and the resulting error observed.

requirements.quote:
PUSH_PROMISE MUST NOT be sent if the SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH setting of
   the peer endpoint is set to 0.  An endpoint that has set this setting
requirements.condition: When the peer endpoint's SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH value is 0
requirements.why_checkable: Frame emission can be checked against the currently effective peer setting.

requirements.quote:
and has received acknowledgment MUST treat the receipt of a
   PUSH_PROMISE frame as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
   PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint has set SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH to 0, received acknowledgment, and then receives PUSH_PROMISE
requirements.error_behavior: Treat receipt as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime test can acknowledge the setting and then inject PUSH_PROMISE to observe the required connection error.

requirements.quote:
PUSH_PROMISE also reserves a stream for later use, causing the
   promised stream to enter the "reserved (local)" or "reserved
   (remote)" state.  A sender MUST NOT send a PUSH_PROMISE on a stream
requirements.condition: When a PUSH_PROMISE reserves a promised stream
requirements.required_behavior: Move the promised stream into the reserved (local) or reserved (remote) state, according to endpoint perspective.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Leave the promised stream in its prior state.
requirements.why_checkable: The promised stream's state can be inspected after processing or sending the frame.

requirements.quote:
(remote)" state.  A sender MUST NOT send a PUSH_PROMISE on a stream
   unless that stream is either "open" or "half-closed (remote)"; the
requirements.condition: When a sender sends PUSH_PROMISE on an associated stream
requirements.required_behavior: The associated stream is open or half-closed (remote).
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send PUSH_PROMISE on an associated stream in any other state.
requirements.why_checkable: The associated stream state can be checked at frame emission time.

requirements.quote:
sender MUST ensure that the promised stream is a valid choice for a
   new stream identifier (Section 5.1.1) (that is, the promised stream
   MUST be in the "idle" state).
requirements.condition: When selecting the promised stream identifier for PUSH_PROMISE
requirements.required_behavior: Select a valid new stream identifier whose stream is in the idle state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Promise a stream that is not idle.
requirements.why_checkable: The selected identifier's stream state can be checked before the frame is sent.

requirements.quote:
treat the receipt of a PUSH_PROMISE on a stream that is neither
   "open" nor "half-closed (local)" as a connection error
   (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.  However, an endpoint that
requirements.condition: When receiving PUSH_PROMISE on an associated stream that is neither open nor half-closed (local)
requirements.error_behavior: Treat receipt as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime test can inject PUSH_PROMISE in each invalid associated-stream state and observe the connection error.

requirements.quote:
has sent RST_STREAM on the associated stream MUST handle PUSH_PROMISE
   frames that might have been created before the RST_STREAM frame is
   received and processed.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint has sent RST_STREAM on the associated stream and receives a PUSH_PROMISE that might predate processing of RST_STREAM
requirements.required_behavior: Handle the potentially in-flight PUSH_PROMISE frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The requirement identifies a race that can be exercised, but does not define the concrete meaning of "handle" or a uniquely required outcome.

requirements.quote:
A receiver MUST treat the receipt of a PUSH_PROMISE that promises an
   illegal stream identifier (Section 5.1.1) as a connection error
   (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.  Note that an illegal stream
requirements.condition: When a received PUSH_PROMISE promises an illegal stream identifier
requirements.error_behavior: Treat receipt as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime test can promise an illegal identifier and observe the required connection error.

requirements.quote:
identifier is an identifier for a stream that is not currently in the
   "idle" state.
requirements.condition: When determining whether a promised stream identifier is illegal
requirements.required_behavior: Classify an identifier for a stream not currently in the idle state as illegal.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Accept a non-idle stream as a legal promised stream identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The identifier's existing stream state can be compared directly with idle.

requirements.quote:
The total number of padding octets is determined by the value of the
   Pad Length field.  If the length of the padding is the length of the
requirements.condition: When a Pad Length field is present
requirements.required_behavior: Use its value as the total number of padding octets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Interpret a different number of octets as padding.
requirements.why_checkable: The declared Pad Length can be compared with the number of octets parsed as padding.

requirements.quote:
frame payload or greater, the recipient MUST treat this as a
   connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When the padding length is greater than or equal to the frame payload length
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the condition as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: Frames at and beyond the padding-length boundary can be injected and the connection error observed.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PING frame header
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the 24-bit Length field as 0x08 and the 8-bit Type field as 0x06.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use another Length or Type value for a valid PING frame.
requirements.why_checkable: Both fixed header field values and their widths are directly inspectable.

requirements.quote:
Unused Flags (7),
     ACK Flag (1),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the PING flags octet
requirements.required_behavior: Represent it as seven unused flag bits and one ACK flag bit.
requirements.why_checkable: The bit allocation of the flags octet is directly inspectable.

requirements.quote:
Reserved (1),
     Stream Identifier (31) = 0,
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PING frame header
requirements.required_behavior: Use one reserved bit and a 31-bit Stream Identifier whose value is 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use a non-zero Stream Identifier for a valid PING frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The field widths and fixed stream identifier value are directly inspectable.

requirements.quote: Opaque Data (64),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PING frame payload
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the opaque data as a 64-bit field.
requirements.why_checkable: The payload field width can be checked directly.

requirements.quote:
In addition to the frame header, PING frames MUST contain 8 octets of
   opaque data in the frame payload.  A sender can include any value it
requirements.condition: For every PING frame
requirements.required_behavior: Include exactly 8 octets of opaque data in the frame payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use a payload length other than 8 octets.
requirements.why_checkable: The PING payload length can be measured directly.

requirements.quote:
opaque data in the frame payload.  A sender can include any value it
   chooses and use those octets in any fashion.
requirements.condition: When selecting the eight opaque-data octets for a PING frame
requirements.required_behavior: Allow any octet values and any sender-defined use.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Impose a protocol-specific value constraint on the opaque data.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can verify that arbitrary 64-bit payload values are transmitted without protocol-level reinterpretation or rejection.

requirements.quote:
Receivers of a PING frame that does not include an ACK flag MUST send
   a PING frame with the ACK flag set in response, with an identical
   frame payload.  PING responses SHOULD be given higher priority than
requirements.condition: When receiving a PING frame without the ACK flag
requirements.required_behavior: Send a PING response with the ACK flag set and a frame payload identical to the received payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Omit the response, leave ACK unset, or alter the response payload.
requirements.why_checkable: A request and response can be compared for response presence, ACK value, and byte-for-byte payload identity.

requirements.quote:
frame payload.  PING responses SHOULD be given higher priority than
   any other frame.
requirements.condition: When scheduling a PING response alongside other frames
requirements.required_behavior: Give the PING response higher priority than any other frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The scheduler's output order or priority assignment can be observed under contention.

requirements.quote:
ACK (0x01):  When set, the ACK flag indicates that this PING frame is
      a PING response.  An endpoint MUST set this flag in PING
requirements.condition: When encoding a PING response
requirements.required_behavior: Set the ACK flag (0x01).
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send a PING response without ACK set.
requirements.why_checkable: The response frame's ACK bit can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote:
responses.  An endpoint MUST NOT respond to PING frames containing
      this flag.
requirements.condition: When receiving a PING frame with the ACK flag set
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send a PING response to that frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime test can inject an ACK-bearing PING and verify that no response is emitted.

requirements.quote:
PING frames are not associated with any individual stream.  If a PING
   frame is received with a Stream Identifier field value other than
   0x00, the recipient MUST respond with a connection error
   (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a PING frame is received with a Stream Identifier other than 0x00
requirements.error_behavior: Respond with a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A PING with a non-zero stream identifier can be injected and the resulting error observed.

requirements.quote:
Receipt of a PING frame with a length field value other than 8 MUST
   be treated as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
   FRAME_SIZE_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a received PING frame has a Length field value other than 8
requirements.error_behavior: Treat receipt as a connection error of type FRAME_SIZE_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: PING frames with invalid declared lengths can be injected and the required connection error observed.
